Team / Samir / Jordan —

Thanks for jumping on this. We’re finalizing the on-site plan for the two-day executive workshop at Acme’s Executive Hub (May 17-18). High-level asks:

- RF/spectrum sweep + signal map for the main control room and adjacent breakout (need pre-check for possible interference).
- Confirm cable paths and rack access windows (will need floor-to-rack elevations for any patching).
- Onsite staffing plan (tech lead + engineers) and proposed arrival/check windows for vendor crew.
- Power draw and UPS recommendations for the mix of cameras, encoders, and meeting-room codec.
- Network test requirements: we expect a bridged media VLAN and a guest SSID for remote panels; please advise test plan and 48-hour smoke test window.

Proposed site-visit window: Thurs, May 5, 09:00–12:00 PT (flexible). Please confirm if you can do a sweep then or suggest an alternate.

I’ve attached a preliminary site map (site_map_prelim.pdf) and the event access matrix we’re working from. Dawn Chang (Acme) is the venue POC — I’ll loop her in after we confirm availability.

Deliverables we’ll need after the visit: short SOW estimate (labor + travel), a list of recommended spare gear, and a 1-page risk summary (RF, power, bandwidth).

Next steps: Samir/Jordan — confirm May 5 availability and send an initial equipment checklist and crew headcount. Marcus/Laura — please confirm whether NetOps will provision a VLAN and whether Security will authorize badge access for vendor crew on event days.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Programs Manager, Redwood Inference

Hi Aisha —

Thanks — we can do the May 5 window (09:00–12:00). Quick observations from satellite view of the floor:

- There’s a telecom riser at the north core that should reach the main control room with a 10m run; plan for two 12-fiber LC tails for redundancy.
- Nearby rooftop HVAC equipment has historically introduced intermittent RF noise in the 2.4GHz band on the east side of the building; recommend a sweep and possibly re-locating two wireless mics to avoid that arc.
- For cameras + encoders + meeting codec, plan for a sustained draw of ~2.2kW; recommend a UPS with 20 minutes runtime at that load for graceful failover.
- Crew: 1 lead engineer (Samir), 1 AV tech, 1 rigger — two-day onsite rate and travel estimate attached.

We’ll bring a spectrum analyzer and our signal-mapper kit. Deliverables after the visit: annotated floor plan with recommended mic placements, rack elevations, and a short SOW with labor/travel. I attached a preliminary estimate (survey_scope_estimate.pdf).

If NetOps can provision the media VLAN and a test SSID 48 hours prior, we can do a full throughput + packet-loss check during the 48-hour smoke window.

—Samir
AVPros, Principal Engineer
samir@avpros.io
Attachments: survey_scope_estimate.pdf (PDF)

Aisha —

Quick network asks from my side:

- NetOps POC: send me the contact so I can confirm VLAN tagging, MTU, and whether jumbo frames are allowed on the media path. We’ll need to reserve a /30 for the codec pair during the tests.
- IP addressing: prefer static addressing for all production encoders.
- QoS: confirm DSCP markings for media; packet prioritization must be tested during the smoke test.

Security: please get an ETA on vendor badge provisioning (temporary badges for Samir’s crew plus access windows). Also confirm whether the venue requires vendor background checks for tech leads.

I’ll coordinate with NetOps once you give me the POC.

Marcus

Marcus / Aisha —

>> Marcus: we can work against whatever VLAN configuration NetOps prefers. For the smoke test we’ll ask that you create a media VLAN and a guest SSID with no captive portal so we can validate RTP streams.

We’ll bring a handheld signal analyzer and a line-power meter; if rooftop HVAC is noisy on the east side we’ll propose mic relocation to the west aisle and add two RF dampers if necessary.

Pre-test checklist I’ll need from NetOps:
- VLAN tag and gateway IP for media VLAN
- Switch port speed, PoE budget (if any end devices are PoE)
- NTP server reachable from event gear for timestamping

I’ve attached our kit checklist for the sweep (site_survey_kit_checklist.pdf). If Dawn (Acme) can grant vendor badge provisioning 48 hours before arrival that will save time on-site.

Samir
